name: Ministry of Home Affairs

scam_info.sample: On 10 August 2026, HTX detected more than 500 fake websites impersonating MHA and Home Team agencies and promptly took steps to take them down. All identified websites were taken down by 11 August 2026.
scam_info.notes: Covers MHA plus 7 agencies (SPF, CNB, SCDF, ICA, SPS, HTX, HTA). Names no domains. Guidance: official sites end with .gov.sg; report via the ScamShield Helpline 1799 or police.gov.sg/i-witness. Republished by SPS on 13 Aug 2026; other agencies did not republish it per their sitemaps.

scam_info.sample: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 | Addressing hotel booking phishing cases involving genuine booking details and obligations of hotels and booking platforms to notify affected customers
scam_info.notes: RSS 2.0 declared via <link rel="alternate"> (fields: title, link, guid, pubDate, category, description). Rolling window of 200 items (6 Jun to 25 Nov 2026); 24 mention scam/fraud/phish/impersonat/fake. Mostly parliamentary replies, speeches and policy (e.g. Sentencing (Scams) Bill, 3 Nov 2026). Few public advisories and almost no IOCs. Sitemap https://www.mha.gov.sg/sitemap.xml (3,543 URLs, lastmod) has 193 keyword slugs (187 newsroom, 103 of them PQ/speech). Many lastmods are a bulk 2026-07-30 re-save, so use the RSS pubDate for dating.

scam_info.sample: To ask the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how many cases of fake bulk order scams impersonating SAF personnel have been reported since May 2025
scam_info.notes: Written PQ answer dated 26 Sep 2025 (JSON-LD shows the 2026-07-30 bulk re-save). Siblings: measures-to-enhance-awareness-of-fake-bulk-order-scams and status-of-investigations-into-fake-bulk-order-scams-involving-impersonation-of-saf-personnel. Relevant to MINDEF/SAF impersonation.

notes: Parent of SPF, SCDF, ICA, CNB, SPS, HTA, HTX, GRA and YRSG (SGDI). MHA SMS exceptions per sms.gov.sg: 70999 (Police emergency SMS), 70995 (SCDF 995 SMS), "MHAalert" (one-way public alerts in demarcated areas; check page lists it as "MHA Alert"). The machine-readable endpoint is the newsroom RSS. Scam content is policy/PQ-heavy with no IOC lists.

name: Singapore Police Force

scam_info.sample: 20261120_two_malaysian_men_to_be_charged_for_their_involvement_in_government_officials_impersonation_scam
scam_info.notes: Main SPF scam-advisory stream; icanactagainstscams.gov.sg /scam-trends is the structured view of the same advisories. Sitemap from robots.txt: 5,170 URLs, priority only, no lastmod. 4,203 news URLs; 990 slugs match scam/fraud/phish/impersonat/fake/hoax/spoof/beware/unsolicited/cyber/malware; 426 contain "advisory"; 375 both (item_count). Slug pattern /media-hub/news/YYYY/MM/YYYYMMDD_title. JSON-LD datePublished on pages. No RSS. The sitemap lags: newest entry 20261106 on 2026-11-26, while the /media-hub/news listing (10 items) showed 20261123 on 2026-11-25. IOC density is low; screenshots are images (72 img tags on the 20260808 advisory), and text links are usually only official domains. robots disallows /api/, /RestApi/, /sitefinity, search.

scam_info.sample: majority of the victims would receive unsolicited Apple iMessage from foreign numbers or email addresses. The messages misled victims into believing that they were from SPF, TP or “District Court”
scam_info.notes: Representative 2026 SPF self-impersonation advisory (SPF, Traffic Police, Singapore Courts via iMessage). Text contains only official/benign domains (support.apple.com, www.courts.gov.sg, www.police.gov.sg, www.scamshield.gov.sg). Scam domains, if shown, are inside images.

scam_info.sample: If you receive an SMS from the government, make sure it is sent from the gov.sg SMS Sender ID*.
scam_info.notes: Awareness hub. Links to the sms.gov.sg/exceptions sender-ID list, the ScamShield GOIS page, the ESSR 1H 2026 and the Anti-Scam Resource Guide via go.gov.sg/resourceguidepamphlet{eng,man,mly,tml}. Sibling pages: /advisories/cybercrime (+ /cybercrime, /hacking-and-website-defacement, /ransomware), /advisories/unlicensed-moneylending, /advisories/misuse-of-sim-card-offences, /knowledge-hub/legislation/caning-for-scams-and-scams-related-offences, /knowledge-hub/legislation/online-harms-act-overview/* (OCHA process; no directions published).

scam_info.sample: all outgoing calls from the SPF will be made from the single caller ID “6000 0999”. Following each call, members of the public will also receive an SMS from the official “gov.sg” SMS sender ID
scam_info.notes: From 2 Nov 2026 SPF is the first agency on a single outgoing caller ID (built with OGP, MDDI and IMDA). 6000 0999 is never used on WhatsApp/Telegram. Jan-Sep 2026: at least 1,310 police-impersonation cases, at least $53.3m lost. Allowlist item.

scam_info.sample: mid-year-scams-and-cybercrime-brief-2026 (redirects to PDF)
scam_info.notes: The sitemap has 20 scams-and-cybercrime brief/statistics URLs (annual 2022-2025 and mid-year 2023-2026, each with an -infographic variant). The page URL redirects to a PDF. Aggregates only (cases, losses, scam types, platforms, disruption counts). The Mid-Year 2026 PDF was created 26 Aug 2026 (per 01_sg_official.md).

scam_info.sample: I-Witness allows anyone to provide information about criminal and/or suspicious activity to the Police.
scam_info.notes: Public tip-off portal. MHA, ICA, GRA and others point fake-site and unlawful-gambling reports here.

scam_info.sample: the-anti-scam-centre---a-collaborative-approach-against-scams
scam_info.notes: No dedicated Anti-Scam Command (ASCom) or Anti-Scam Centre (ASC) landing page exists in the sitemap. ASCom and ASC appear only in news and Police Life items, e.g. 20220906_opening_of_anti-scam_command_office (ASCom operationalised 22 Mar 2022), 20260707_anti_scam_centre_and_five_banks_collaborate..., and 20260703_spf_forms_new_cyber_command... (ASC now inside the Cyber Command, from 3 Jul 2026). Police Life (613 URLs) also has anti-scam features. The ASC feature page and 20260703 Cyber Command release were fetched (both 200). The others are known from the sitemap and search only.

hotlines: 6000 0999 (single outgoing caller ID for all SPF calls from 2 Nov 2026)

notes: Most-impersonated agency (SPF brand tag, 5 advisories; sample scam domains include policegov.eu.cc). SPF is the de facto central advisory publisher for most brands. Its operational IOC sets (National Scams List, SATIS takedowns, OCHA directions) are not published. SMS exceptions per sms.gov.sg: 70999 (emergency SMS), 80709999 (Police NS mobilisation; previously 83385761), "POLICE 999" (emergency video link / silent-call advisory). Since 1 Jan 2025 SPF also blocks unlawful remote-gambling sites (taken over from GRA); those block lists are not published.

name: ScamShield

scam_info.sample: Scammers are sending fake text messages notifying people that their OCBC cards have been suspended. ... 🔎 SMSes from OCBC should reflect OCBC as the Sender ID.
scam_info.notes: NEW since the 2026-11-25 survey: RSS 2.0 declared via rel=alternate (the site migrated to a Next.js Isomer build with JSON-LD). 10 items (28 Aug to 20 Nov 2026); older alerts rotate out. Brand-level alerts (OCBC, SingHealth Polyclinics, OneMotoring, couriers, telco staff, fake SPF "scam recovery" ads) with guidance only: no URLs, phones or sender IDs except official ones. Item URL pattern /resources/scam-alert/alert-DDmonYY/. The sitemap (88 URLs, lastmod) also works for change detection.

scam_info.sample: Monthly Scams Bulletin Issue 11- November 2026 [PDF, 3.8 MB]
scam_info.notes: RSS of PDF bulletins: 88 items (23 Mar 2023 to 20 Nov 2026). PDFs are hosted on isomer-user-content.by.gov.sg. Trend/statistics content with no IOCs. The 2026 series now runs to Issue 11 (Nov); the survey had seen only Jan-Mar.

scam_info.sample: E-Commerce Scams Situation Report (ESSR) 1H 2026
scam_info.notes: Platform-level e-commerce scam rankings (cases and losses by platform). Useful as a platform prior, not as IOCs. Semi-annual.

scam_info.notes: Single caller ID announcement (allowlist).

scam_info.notes: Phone allowlist of 8 banks' anti-scam hotlines: DBS/POSB 1800 339 6963 / +65 6339 6963; OCBC 6363 3333 (press 8); UOB 6255 0160; Citibank 6337 5519; CIMB 6333 7777; HSBC 1800 472 2669 / +65 6472 2669; Maybank 1800 629 2265 / +65 6533 5229; Standard Chartered 6747 7000. scam_info.sample: If you received an SMS from the government, make sure it is sent from the gov.sg SMS Sender ID.
scam_info.notes: GOIS explainer (SPF/MAS/MOM impersonation, safe accounts, meet-up handovers). Sibling scam-type pages under /learn-to-recognise-scams/ cover e-commerce, job, phishing, fake-friend, loan, insurance-service, internet-love, sexual-service, crypto, tech-support and investment scams (sitemap, lastmod May-Jun 2026).

scam_info.notes: Pointers to official registers: MAS FID, Register of Representatives and Investor Alert List; CEA Public Register; and others for jobs and property.

scam_info.sample: Call the 24/7 ScamShield Helpline at 1799 if you are unsure if something is a scam.
scam_info.notes: Hub. Report and check channels: ScamShield app, 1799 helpline, go.gov.sg/scamreport and the WhatsApp bot (go.gov.sg/scamshield-bot per survey). These give per-query verdicts only; no list or API. Sitemap: 88 URLs with lastmod (robots allows all except /search). Homepage links scamvaccine.gov.sg (waitlist) and icanactagainstscams.gov.sg.

notes: Joint SPF/NCPC/OGP suite (Sept 2024) that absorbed NCPC ScamAlert. Re-verified 2026-11-26: www.scamalert.sg and scamalert.sg return 301 to https://www.scamshield.gov.sg/, and www.scamshield.org.sg returns 302 to the same. Two documented RSS feeds now exist (scam-alert, scam-bulletins), but neither carries IOCs. Parent set to police.gov.sg because SPF leads the programme. Related: icanactagainstscams.gov.sg (structured SPF advisories; already ingested, not re-done here) and scamvaccine.gov.sg (linked, not visited).

name: Singapore Civil Defence Force

scam_info.sample: An example of such a fake email address is “quotation@scdf-gov-sg.com”. All SCDF email accounts end with @scdf.gov.sg.
scam_info.notes: News release 12 Aug 2020: fake procurement emails to companies from an individual posing as an SCDF officer. Fake address is behind Cloudflare email-obfuscation (data-cfemail), decoded = quotation@scdf-gov-sg.com. Says SCDF invites quotations/tenders only via GeBIZ. Duplicate URL also indexed at https://scdf.gov.sg/eventslisting/newsarticledetail/individual-posing-as-an-scdf-officer-to-procure-items

scam_info.sample: The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) has received public feedback about companies claiming to be endorsed by the SCDF to sell fire extinguishers and/ or first aid kits.
scam_info.notes: Fire-extinguisher/first-aid-kit door-to-door sales scam. No company names. States SCDF does not sell these items, has authorised no company, and residents will not be fined for not having them.

scam_info.sample: In some instances, the sales personnel had shown their company pass with photo identification or the Civil Defence Emergency Handbook, to give the impression that they were representing the SCDF. Some even threatened to issue fines
scam_info.notes: Same text also at .../newsarticledetail/Alert-on-Unauthorised-Business-Activities (no year suffix; fetched 2026-11-26 HTTP 200, dated 25 July 2016). Adds that SCDF house-to-house SGSecure visits never compel purchases.

scam_info.sample: The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) has received a number of complaints about companies claiming to be endorsed by the SCDF to sell fire extinguishers and/ or conduct fire safety talks to the public.
scam_info.notes: Impersonation of SCDF officers in hard-sell of extinguishers, fire insurance and fire-safety talks. Explains verification: uniformed regulars carry a warrant card, NSFs an NS identity card.

scam_info.sample: a woman had impersonated as a SCDF officer and tried to sell a fire extinguisher to his father. The complainant also claimed that the impersonator had mentioned that SCDF would provide $30,000 worth of fire insurance
scam_info.notes: Byte-identical text (dated 23 December 2011) also at ...-SCDF-Officer-2011 (fetched 2026-11-26 HTTP 200). A third variant URL ...-SCDF-Officer-231211 appears under /eventslisting/ in search results.

scam_info.sample: The SCDF has received a number of complaints in the past month about companies claiming to be endorsed by us to sell fire extinguishers and/or conduct fire safety talks to the public.
scam_info.notes: Earliest SCDF alert on endorsement and impersonation sales scams.

scam_info.sample: With effect from 1st June 2017, the Singapore Civil Defence Force"s (SCDF) emergency hotline number "995" will be displayed on telephones" caller ID.
scam_info.notes: Official-caller-ID allowlist item: SCDF Operations Centre call-backs show "995". Not shown for international numbers. The page also warns about numbers beginning with the "+995" prefix (Georgia country code), which are not SCDF.

scam_info.sample: SCDF does not endorse or certify products. Legitimate fire safety products are certified by independent accredited Certification Bodies. Claims of 'SCDF-approved' or similar are false. Report them at https://www.scdf.gov.sg/home/feedback .
scam_info.notes: The sample is a site-wide notification banner on every scdf.gov.sg page (seen 2026-11-25/26). It is the only current (2026) SCDF anti-scam statement; the alert pages are 2010-2020. Sitemap (from robots.txt) has 1,228 URLs, 485 newsarticledetail, and no lastmod. The listing is a filter UI with no RSS. Latest date is the newest 'Discover more' news release seen (24 Sep 2026). There is no scam category; the 7 scam/impersonation items were found by slug/keyword. The banner also announces that the SCDF Hotline 1800 280 0000 ceases on 21 Dec 2026.

hotlines: 995 (emergency; shown as caller ID "995" on SCDF call-backs since 1 Jun 2017)
1800-286-5555 (SCDF general enquiries, cited in older impersonation alerts)
emails: *@scdf.gov.sg (per SCDF, all SCDF email accounts end with @scdf.gov.sg)

notes: User priority. SCDF publishes no scam list, RSS or dedicated scam section. Its scam info is (a) 7 legacy alert pages (2010-2020) on fire-extinguisher, first-aid-kit, fire-insurance and fire-safety-talk door-to-door sales falsely claiming SCDF endorsement or impersonating SCDF officers, plus one fake-procurement-email case (the only concrete IOC: quotation@scdf-gov-sg.com), and (b) a current site-wide 'SCDF-approved claims are false' banner. Fake SCDF calls/SMS: no SCDF page found. SCDF was named among the 7 Home Team agencies in the MHA advisory of 12 Aug 2026 on >500 fake look-alike sites, which names no domains (see mha.gov.sg). Related SPF release 25 Jul 2023 (https://www.police.gov.sg/media-hub/news/2023/07/20230725_four_men_to_be_charged_for_false_and_misleading_claims_and_for_obstruction_of_justice): door-to-door seller 'Fire Safety Prevention SG (FSP)' falsely claimed SCDF would summon households without an extinguisher. SMS exceptions per sms.gov.sg: 70995, 80709995 (NS call-ups; previously 91449746), 'SCDF 995' (emergency video link). All other SCDF SMS come from gov.sg.

scam_info.notes: Undated advisory on scams and phishing (fake voter-roll removal notices, chat-app scam links, fake surveys). Search results also say ELD officer calls do not start with "+65". robots.txt returned nothing and /sitemap.xml returned 403 (2026-11-25), so the page was found via WebSearch.

notes: Narrative only.

scam_info.notes: Spoofed official number.

scam_info.sample: mfa-spokesmans-comments-in-response-to-media-queries-on-callers-impersonating-mfa-officers-in-scam-c-22-apr-2015
scam_info.notes: Plus a follow-up dated 11 May 2015. Also 2026-11-19 "statement-of-principles-of-the-contact-group-on-countering-criminal-online-scams-and-scam-centers" (policy). Sitemap 8,786 URLs; only 6 strict scam slugs. Overseas missions (Overseas Missions in SGDI) were not crawled.

notes: Low volume. Consular/fake-embassy scams are mostly reported via SPF advisories. Embassy sites (mfa.gov.sg/<mission>) were not individually checked.

name: Ministry of Defence / Singapore Armed Forces
notes: Sitemap (5,711 URLs, lastmod) has 0 strict scam/fraud/phish/impersonat/fake/hoax/spoof slugs. The broad-keyword hits are "cyber"/"alert" pages, not scams. MINDEF's Sep 2025 warnings on fake bulk-order scams by people posing as SAF personnel were posted on social media (per news search), not on mindef.gov.sg. MHA PQ replies cover them (see mha.gov.sg). SMS 72255 is the official NS two-way sender ID.
